Application process
Follow the steps below to prepare your application. You can submit your application anytime, but if you’re applying for a competitive scholarship, make sure you know the closing date.
Applications will be closed if they:
do not meet UTS English language requirements*
do not include evidence of agreed supervision
are missing required documents (including correctly certified documents) at the time of application
The UTS Graduate Research School (GRS) will not follow up on missing or incorrectly certified documents.
Applications submitted after the scholarship application closing date will not be considered for the UTS competitive scholarship, but may be assessed for candidature.
*Please note: International applicants: the Medium of Instruction (MoI) option is not accepted for qualifications from India, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Pakistan.
Before you apply
To be able to apply for a research degree, check the details and create a plan that’s right for you.
Check the eligibility criteria for research degrees.
Explore scholarships and funding.
Understand fees and costs.
Understand the Australian student visa process.
Step 1: Find your research topic
UTS research delivers real-world impact that makes a difference to the world we live in. What problem will you tackle?
Explore UTS research.
Search for and contact a supervisor with expertise in your field.
Check whether your faculty has pre-admission requirements.
Learn more about writing your research proposal.
Step 2: Prepare your application
Submitting your application is easier if you’ve prepared everything in advance.
Check application closing dates.
Write your research proposal.
Prepare your documents.
What to expect in the application form
If you have prepared your documents, the application form will take approximately 20 minutes to complete.
In the application form, you’ll be asked to provide the following proof:
eligibility criteria
English language requirements*
confirmed funding or that you can financially support yourself
completed pre-admission requirements
evidence of supervisory agreement, and
identity/citizenship.
You’ll also be asked if:
you are represented by a UTS authorised agent
you would like to be considered for a UTS competitive scholarship, and
you have an existing relationship or affiliation with UTS.
Once you register an account for the UTS Student Portal, you can save and complete your application at any time.
*Please note that the Medium of Instruction (MoI) option is not accepted for qualifications from India, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Pakistan. Applicants with qualifications from these countries will need to provide a valid IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, or UTS College Academic English score.
How to submit your application
IMPORTANT: The application portal will be closed at 9am, 02 November 2026 AEDT as we transition to a new application form to be launched in mid to late January 2027. In the interim no new or incomplete applications can be submitted.
All complete applications submitted before 02 November 2026 will be assessed before the end of 2026. Incomplete applications will be deleted.
Use Google Chrome as your internet browser.
Register a Future Student account in the UTS Student Portal.
Activate your account by clicking the link in the verification email.
Set up multifactor authentication when prompted.
Once you’re logged in, select Apply for a course.
Choose Higher degree research.
Follow the prompts to complete your application and submit all documents.
Submit now
After you apply
We’ll send you an email to confirm that we’ve received your application.
How we’ll notify you of the outcome
You’ll receive an email confirming the outcome of your application. While this process usually takes 12 weeks, factors out of our control may delay a decision.
Successful applications
If your application has been successful, you’ll receive a letter of offer via email. It will include:
your suggested start date
your UTS student number
your scholarship status, if applicable, and
information on how to accept your offer.
Upon accepting your offer, we will provide you with a confirmation of enrolment (CoE) so you can apply for a student visa in the Postgraduate Research Sector for the full duration of your course.
How to accept your offer
Unsuccessful applications
If your application has been unsuccessful and you would like feedback, contact the faculty or institute you applied to.
Track your application
The UTS Student Portal is your main source of information during this time.
In the portal you can track the progress of your application.
